description: §5.2 rule 3 (S457), the parenthesized expression form `href=(@cell)`: a URL attribute whose value is a cell read is judged at runtime on every write — a non-admitted scheme writes about:blank (initially and on a reactive re-write); relative URLs, a raster data:image on an image source, and a `data` attribute outside <object> are written unchanged. Written in forms both implementations compile (s462-bootstrap-sink-guards — the bootstrap's twin of url-data-scheme-runtime-guard, whose `${…}` forms the bootstrap does not parse; the bare `href=@cell` form is not used because impl#1 writes it as the static cell NAME — g-unquoted-href-cell-ref-renders-cell-name-s456).
rationale: §5.2 rule 3: covered writes include "(ii) every non-literal value — `href=${expr}`, `href=@cell` where it binds, …"; "The write is judged when the element is built AND on every reactive re-write when a dependency changes." Leading C0 controls and spaces are ignored and the scheme compares case-insensitively. Element scope: `action` (`form`), `data` (`object`) — "An attribute the HTML standard makes URL-valued only on particular elements is covered only there". Admitted: no scheme, http/https/ftp/mailto/tel/sms, and a raster data:image only on an image-source attribute; "Any other value SHALL be written as `about:blank`".
